# Evidence

<!-- Generated by `pnpm evidence --write` from docs/evidence.json. Don't edit this file: edit the JSON and regenerate. -->

214 claims quoted from the README and the docs, each paired with the code that does it and with what checks it: a test in this repository, a read-only call to NEAR mainnet or the live site, or both. Not every sentence in those documents has a row; the rows are the claims a script can check. The source is [evidence.json](evidence.json); [`scripts/evidence.mjs`](../scripts/evidence.mjs) checks all of it.

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm evidence            # every claim's code pointers and tests: no network, no keys, no env
pnpm evidence --chain    # also the read-only checks against NEAR mainnet and the live site
pnpm evidence --only track-pricing-file,track-merchant-broke   # just these claims
pnpm evidence --json     # the same result as one JSON object
```

**What a line means.** `PASS` is mechanical: the claim's quote is still in its document, each code pointer's anchor text is still in its file exactly once, each named test is still declared in its file and passed just now, and (with `--chain`) each read-only check answered as expected. It does not judge whether the test is a good proof of the sentence; that is what review is for, and each row names its test so it can be read. `FAIL`: one of those didn't hold; the line says which. `SKIP`: the proof couldn't run here, and the line says why (no `cargo`, offline, a rate limit, or a claim that rests on the chain run without `--chain`). A claim proven by tests passes on its tests; if it also has a chain check, that runs with `--chain`. The script exits 1 on any `FAIL` and 0 otherwise, and ends with one summary line.

**Coverage.** 187 of 214 rows cite a test (368 different tests); 105 have a read-only chain or site check (48 checks); 0 have only a code pointer. All 317 code pointers are anchored. Offline the script ends `214 claims: 151 PASS, 0 FAIL, 63 SKIP.`; with `--chain`, `214 claims: 214 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP.` when every endpoint answers.

**What a status means.** A status says how far the proof reaches, and it is set by hand to the weakest true reading.

| Status | Meaning | Claims |
|---|---|---|
| `proven by test` | A test in this repo asserts the claim, and at least one of the cited tests runs the code that does it: the simulation, the server on an in-memory database, the contract, a script. Other tests cited beside it may only read text. Runs offline. | 103 |
| `pinned by test` | Every cited test only reads: it compares the document's words with source text, a constant, a config file or a lockfile, and runs none of the behaviour. It fails when the two drift apart; it does not show the code works. Runs offline. | 8 |
| `proven on chain` | A read-only call to NEAR mainnet shows it: contract state, or a transaction that happened. Needs `--chain`. | 45 |
| `live check` | A read-only request to the live site (or a third-party index of the chain) shows it. Needs `--chain`. | 18 |
| `checked in git` | This clone's own commit history shows it: an order of commits, a date, a branch. Runs offline; skipped, with a note, in a clone without that history. | 4 |
| `simulation only` | True in the simulated market or the economy lab, and tested there. Not something mainnet does. | 24 |
| `built, off on mainnet` | The code and its tests are here, and it is switched off or not yet triggered on mainnet. | 3 |
| `owner action needed` | Only the owner can make it true (a transaction, a setting or a deploy). The pointer shows what is ready. | 9 |

Line numbers below are computed from a short piece of text in each file (the anchor in evidence.json). If the code moves, `pnpm evidence --check` fails until this file is regenerated; if the text is gone, the claim fails.

## How verification works

| Claim | Code | Test | Run | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="verify-one-sim"></a>packages/game-core is a deterministic simulation: a 60 Hz fixed step, trig-free maths (polynomial sin, cos and atan2 in packages/game-core/src/sim3d/dmath.ts), and integer HP and score.<br><sub>README · `verify-one-sim`</sub> | [`packages/game-core/src/sim3d/constants.ts:17`](../packages/game-core/src/sim3d/constants.ts#L17)<br>[`packages/game-core/src/sim3d/dmath.ts:8`](../packages/game-core/src/sim3d/dmath.ts#L8) | `packages/game-core/test/dmath.test.ts`: “dsin and dcos match the platform within 1e-13 over ±200 radians”<br>`packages/game-core/test/score.test.ts`: “pays 1,000 × levelScale for a fight, half again for a boss, in integers”<br>`packages/game-core/test/determinism.test.ts`: “the same log gives the same hash, checkpoints and score, twice and after other runs” | `pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/dmath.test.ts -t 'dsin and dcos match the platform within 1e-13 over ±200 radians'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/score.test.ts -t 'pays 1,000 × levelScale for a fight, half again for a boss, in integers'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/determinism.test.ts -t 'the same log gives the same hash, checkpoints and score, twice and after other runs'` | `proven by test` |
| <a id="verify-scan"></a>A test scans it for sources of non-determinism.<br><sub>README · `verify-scan`</sub> | [`packages/game-core/test/determinism-scan.test.ts:25`](../packages/game-core/test/determinism-scan.test.ts#L25) | `packages/game-core/test/determinism-scan.test.ts`: “catches each banned form and ignores comments and strings”<br>`packages/game-core/test/determinism-scan.test.ts`: “finds none of them in src/rules, src/sim3d or src/input” | `pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/determinism-scan.test.ts -t 'catches each banned form and ignores comments and strings'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/determinism-scan.test.ts -t 'finds none of them in src/rules, src/sim3d or src/input'` | `proven by test` |
| <a id="verify-recording"></a>They're run-length encoded, usually 1–5 KB a night; the server refuses a log over 64 KB.<br><sub>README · `verify-recording`</sub><br><sub>The README said 2–15 KB. The recorded nights are 0.3 to 2.1 KB and the live top-of-board logs were 1.1 to 4.1 KB on Nov 12, so it now says 1–5 KB.</sub> | [`packages/game-core/src/input/log.ts:27`](../packages/game-core/src/input/log.ts#L27)<br>[`apps/wgp/src/server/verify.ts:34`](../apps/wgp/src/server/verify.ts#L34) | `packages/game-core/test/input-log.test.ts`: “run-length encodes a held input to a few bytes”<br>`packages/game-core/test/input-log.test.ts`: “rejects every truncation and any trailing byte”<br>`apps/wgp/src/evidence/readme-numbers.test.ts`: “the recorded nights' input logs are inside the size the README gives”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/verify.test.ts`: “refuses another ruleset, an empty log and a log over 64 KB before replaying anything” | `pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/input-log.test.ts -t 'run-length encodes a held input to a few bytes'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/input-log.test.ts -t 'rejects every truncation and any trailing byte'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/evidence/readme-numbers.test.ts -t "the recorded nights' input logs are inside the size the README gives"`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/verify.test.ts -t 'refuses another ruleset, an empty log and a log over 64 KB before replaying anything'` | `proven by test` |
| <a id="verify-start"></a>POST /api/runs/start issues a server-signed seed. A player has at most one active run and 20 ranked runs a day.<br><sub>README · `verify-start`</sub> | [`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.ts:50`](../apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.ts#L50)<br>[`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.ts:44`](../apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.ts#L44) | `apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.test.ts`: “issues a run with an HMAC seed, the ruleset and the save revision”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.test.ts`: “allows one run in flight, unless the old one is abandoned”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.test.ts`: “caps a player at 20 runs a UTC day” | `pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/runs.test.ts -t 'issues a run with an HMAC seed, the ruleset and the save revision'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/runs.test.ts -t 'allows one run in flight, unless the old one is abandoned'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/runs.test.ts -t 'caps a player at 20 runs a UTC day'` | `proven by test` |

Each mode has its own ruleset tag (cases, trials, the City), so a log from one mode never replays as another.<br><sub>README · `verify-rulesets`</sub> | [`packages/game-core/src/sim3d/constants.ts:14`](../packages/game-core/src/sim3d/constants.ts#L14)<br>[`packages/game-core/src/replay.ts:243`](../packages/game-core/src/replay.ts#L243) | `packages/game-core/test/golden.test.ts`: “are pinned to this ruleset”<br>`packages/game-core/test/trial.test.ts`: “number every course's logs apart from each other, the patrol's and the chapter's”<br>`packages/game-core/test/case-golden.test.ts`: “is refused as a patrol night, and a patrol golden as a chapter”<br>`packages/game-core/test/roam-golden.test.ts`: “is refused by the night verifier and the chapter verifier”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/compete.test.ts`: “refuses another mode's log, and another course's”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/cases.test.ts`: “refuses a patrol log for a chapter run, and a chapter log for a ranked night” | `pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/golden.test.ts -t 'are pinned to this ruleset'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/trial.test.ts -t "number every course's logs apart from each other, the patrol's and the chapter's"`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/case-golden.test.ts -t 'is refused as a patrol night, and a patrol golden as a chapter'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/roam-golden.test.ts -t 'is refused by the night verifier and the chapter verifier'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/compete.test.ts -t "refuses another mode's log, and another course's"`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/cases.test.ts -t 'refuses a patrol log for a chapter run, and a chapter log for a ranked night'` | `proven by test` |

## Limits and what's next

| Claim | Code | Test | Run | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="limits-bots"></a>The server refuses a night handed in faster than real time and caps ranked nights at 20 a day per player; within that cap, nothing stops a bot or a player re-rolling seeds.<br><sub>README · `limits-bots`</sub><br><sub>The two tests show the two limits: game time ahead of the wall clock is refused, and a 21st ranked start in a UTC day is refused. The README used to end "but a patient bot can still play", which understated it: the next two rows show the shipped bot outscores most players and a seed can be re-rolled.</sub> | [`apps/wgp/src/server/verify.ts:32`](../apps/wgp/src/server/verify.ts#L32) | `apps/wgp/src/server/verify.test.ts`: “refuses game time more than 5 seconds ahead of the wall clock, and takes it once the clock catches up”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.test.ts`: “caps a player at 20 runs a UTC day” | `pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/verify.test.ts -t 'refuses game time more than 5 seconds ahead of the wall clock, and takes it once the clock catches up'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/runs.test.ts -t 'caps a player at 20 runs a UTC day'` | `proven by test` |
| <a id="limits-bot-scores"></a>The bot that ships in this repository (packages/game-core/src/sim3d/bot.ts) scores 8,245, 8,350 and 8,870 on the three recorded nights it clears<br><sub>README · `limits-bot-scores`</sub><br><sub>The golden tests replay the bot's recorded nights to those scores (packages/game-core/test/golden/hashes.json), and the app's replay test has the server verify and rank a bot-played night. The pin test holds the README's three numbers to hashes.json. The comparison beside it (on Nov 14, only two players had an All-time best above the lowest of those) is dated, read from GET /api/leaderboard?board=alltime, and has no check.</sub> | [`packages/game-core/src/sim3d/bot.ts:393`](../packages/game-core/src/sim3d/bot.ts#L393) | `packages/game-core/test/golden.test.ts`: “night-1-standard: a first night with the starter powers”<br>`packages/game-core/test/golden.test.ts`: “night-4-heavy: level-2 villains, web bomb, validator slam and front-run”<br>`packages/game-core/test/golden.test.ts`: “night-9-mixed: level-5 villains, Fork, ZK cloak and gas refund”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/real-replay.test.ts`: “verifies a bot-played night, saves it and ranks it”<br>`apps/wgp/src/evidence/readme-numbers.test.ts`: “the bot's scores under Limits are the recorded nights' own, the ones the bot clears” | `pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/golden.test.ts -t 'night-1-standard: a first night with the starter powers'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/golden.test.ts -t 'night-4-heavy: level-2 villains, web bomb, validator slam and front-run'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/golden.test.ts -t 'night-9-mixed: level-5 villains, Fork, ZK cloak and gas refund'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/real-replay.test.ts -t 'verifies a bot-played night, saves it and ranks it'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/evidence/readme-numbers.test.ts -t "the bot's scores under Limits are the recorded nights' own, the ones the bot clears"` | `proven by test` |
| <a id="limits-reroll"></a>A player can also abandon a ranked night and start again on a new seed, and the seed decides the night's stops.<br><sub>README · `limits-reroll`</sub><br><sub>Abandoning expires the run in flight and issues a new run, whose seed is an HMAC of its new id; the patrol is a function of that seed alone. Each start counts against the 20 a day.</sub> | [`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.ts:113`](../apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.ts#L113) | `apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.test.ts`: “allows one run in flight, unless the old one is abandoned”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.test.ts`: “issues a run with an HMAC seed, the ruleset and the save revision”<br>`apps/wgp/src/server/db/runs.test.ts`: “caps a player at 20 runs a UTC day”<br>`packages/game-core/test/engine-seed.test.ts`: “with a seed, the patrol is a function of that seed alone” | `pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/runs.test.ts -t 'allows one run in flight, unless the old one is abandoned'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/runs.test.ts -t 'issues a run with an HMAC seed, the ruleset and the save revision'`<br>`pnpm --filter wgp exec vitest run src/server/db/runs.test.ts -t 'caps a player at 20 runs a UTC day'`<br>`pnpm --filter @wgp/game-core exec vitest run test/engine-seed.test.ts -t 'with a seed, the patrol is a function of that seed alone'` | `proven by test` |

## Read-only checks

What `--chain` runs. Each is a view call, a lookup of a transaction that already happened, or a GET; the `git` ones read this clone's history and run offline too. None sends a transaction or needs a key. The command under each is the same request by hand. Counts are checked as lower bounds, and the bound is read from the document's own text when the check runs, so the number is written in one place. A check on something that changes on a known date (the season's record) asserts the right thing in each state. A check on something the deployed contract lacks (a method) fails the day that changes, which is the signal to update the claim.

### <a id="check-market-state"></a>market-state

The contract's market: open, a 2% fee, no Bits cost for crafting, the listing bounds and caps, and eight pools held by the contract's own account. Used by [`track-npc-wallets`](#track-npc-wallets), [`judge-3`](#judge-3), [`economy-trade`](#economy-trade), [`economy-burn-fee`](#economy-burn-fee), [`economy-craft-burn`](#economy-craft-burn), [`near-market-guards`](#near-market-guards), [`status-used`](#status-used), [`limits-craft-bits`](#limits-craft-bits), [`econdoc-not-applied`](#econdoc-not-applied), [`arch-abuse-guards`](#arch-abuse-guards).

```bash
curl -s https://rpc.mainnet.fastnear.com -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"query","params":{"request_type":"call_function","finality":"final","account_id":"game.wgpnear.near","method_name":"market_state","args_base64":"e30="}}' \
  | jq -r '.result.result | implode' | jq .
```

Expected:

- `vendor` is `"game.wgpnear.near"`
- `params.open` is `true`
- `params.fee_bps` is `200`
- `params.craft_bits` is `"0"`
- `params.floor_bps` is `5000`
- `params.ceiling_bps` is `40000`
- `params.max_amount` is `20`
- `params.daily_trades` is `40`
- `pools.length` is `8`
- `prices_milli.length` is `8`

```

- something in `pools.*.item` matches `/^fee-bomb$/`

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'https://www.wgponnear.fun/api/seasons/s1/results'
```

Expected:

- one of three states, each checked in full. Open: `get_season` is `null` and the results file is a 404. Closed: still `null`, and the site serves the frozen results. Recorded: `get_season` has a root, a digest and 1 to 10 accounts; the results file has that root, its sha256 is that digest, its first leaves are those accounts in order, and each holds `trophy:s1:<rank>`. Before 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000Z only the open state passes.
